text: Designing a good REST API requires careful planning. First, define clear, resource-based endpoints, such as `/users` or `/orders`, using nouns instead of verbs. Always use standard HTTP status codes to communicate results: `200` for success, `201` for creation, `404` for not found, and `500` for server errors. Comprehensive documentation is essential, as it helps developers understand how to use your API quickly. Finally, implement versioning from the start—for example, by adding `/v1/` to your URL—so you can make changes later without breaking existing clients. A well-designed API saves time for everyone and builds trust with its users.
